title: Knowledge check: Installing R

questions.prompt: For “Installing R”, which approach best supports a reliable result?
options: Inspect assumptions, run a small example, and verify an edge case.
Trust the first output without inspecting its inputs.
Hide warnings and skip validation to make the result look clean.
Change several unrelated parts at once so the cause of any result is unclear.
questions.answer_key: Inspect assumptions, run a small example, and verify an edge case.
questions.explanation: Use a repeatable setup and verify the toolchain before interpreting an example. Reliable work makes assumptions visible and checks behavior before scaling up.

questions.prompt: Which item is explicitly listed under “Installing R” in the source curriculum?
options: Downloading R from the Official R Project
Change unrelated settings before checking the input
Assume one example proves every edge case
Skip validation when the output looks plausible
questions.answer_key: Downloading R from the Official R Project
questions.explanation: The source PDF lists “Downloading R from the Official R Project” as part of lesson 6. The lesson retains the original topic wording.

questions.prompt: When applying “Installing R” to real work, what should you do before relying on the result?
options: Validate inputs and output shape, test a boundary case, and state limitations.
Assume missing and malformed inputs never occur.
Use the same method regardless of data type or the research question.
Remove inconvenient observations without recording the decision.
questions.answer_key: Validate inputs and output shape, test a boundary case, and state limitations.
questions.explanation: Record the R version, working directory and packages used, then verify one small expression. Record assumptions and known limitations instead of presenting a demonstration as proof.

answer_key_visibility: Server-side only; API should return prompts/options without answer keys or explanations.
